clue.text: Fish unaccompanied

explanation.surface: Someone notes a fish swimming alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a flatfish species, and an adjective meaning single or solitary.

clue.text: Cabinet's performance on occasion

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed on top of the next comes first

parts.note: a show is a performance or entertainment
a case is an instance or occasion, as in 'in that case'

explanation.surface: A government cabinet's showing on some particular occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests government ministers, but here it is a glass display cabinet.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass-fronted display cabinet for exhibiting objects is called by this name.

clue.text: Sort of spin from Labour's leader, say, prior to recess

indicators.note: the earlier pieces come before the next one in the answer
a word's leader is its first letter, here the start of Labour's

parts.note: say signals an example, abbreviated e.g.
a break is a recess or pause, as in Parliament

explanation.surface: Political spin from the Labour leader just before Parliament's recess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' looks political, but it is cricket bowling.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a type of spin delivery turning from leg side to off is given this name.

clue.text: Fear rugby players in Barnet?

definitions.note: Cockney rhyming slang: Barnet Fair = hair, so a barnet is a hairstyle; the question mark marks this as an example

parts.note: dread is great fear
locks are second-row forwards in a rugby scrum

explanation.surface: Fearsome rugby forwards turn up in the north London town of Barnet.
explanation.walkthrough: Barnet reads as the London borough, but in rhyming slang it means a head of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Matted, rope-like strands of hair are an example of a hairstyle, which is what barnet means in slang.

clue.text: Starts to row up River Avon, largely in the countryside

indicators.note: the starts of the following five words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Rowing upstream on the River Avon through mostly rural scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural is an adjective describing things located away from towns, out in farmland.

clue.text: Dismay when old Oscar mounted horse

parts.note: to appal is to dismay

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the pieces go upwards, so they read backwards

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone was dismayed when an elderly man named Oscar climbed onto a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A spotted breed of horse from North America bears this name.

clue.text: Good money given by member, tip included in change

indicators.note: the limb is supplied first, followed by the rest

parts.note: a leg is a limb, or member of the body

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other word, within its letters

parts.note: to alter is to change
an end is a tip

explanation.surface: A club member hands over good money with a gratuity added to the change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' suggests a gratuity left with the change; it is really the end of something, and 'included in' slots it into the middle of the word for change.
explanation.definitionFit: Currency that must legally be accepted in payment is valid money, so good in that sense.

clue.text: Run off to fix an awning

indicators.note: the article is fixed inside the other word

parts.note: to run off copies is to print or copy them

explanation.surface: Someone dashes off to put up an awning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run off' looks like leaving; it means copy, as on a printer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are overhead coverings of cloth that give shelter or shade, so the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Drink readily available after close of innings

indicators.note: the second piece follows the first
the close of a word is its final letter, here of innings

parts.note: handy means close at hand, readily available

explanation.surface: A cricketer wants a drink near at hand when the innings ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A mix of beer and lemonade is a familiar British pub drink.

clue.text: Bess's partner heading off for wild party

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, is taken off

parts.note: Porgy and Bess is Gershwin's opera, so Porgy partners Bess

explanation.surface: Bess's partner leaves for a wild party.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild party is an unrestrained revel, an orgiastic gathering.

clue.text: Advertising material — correct look being discussed

indicators.note: spoken in discussion, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: proper means correct, and a gander is a look

explanation.surface: People discuss whether an advert has the right look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Proper gander' said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Promotional material spreading a message, often biased, is a loose sense of publicity.

clue.text: Sweet artist fed to animal

indicators.note: the artist goes into the animal, as food goes in

parts.note: a camel is an animal
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter is eaten by a beast, like a sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: A chewy confection of boiled sugar and butter is a kind of sweet, or candy.

clue.text: They may bring partners together, like Bryant & May perhaps

definitions.meaning: Bryant & May was a famous British manufacturer of matches

explanation.surface: Bryant and May sound like a pair of matchmaking friends.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both people who pair off couples and firms that make matchsticks.

clue.text: Leaf from notebook taken by girl

indicators.note: the girl takes the notebook, so the notebook follows her

parts.note: Lily is a girl's name
a pad is a notebook

explanation.surface: A girl tears a page from a notebook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf' suggests a page, but it is the floating leaf of a water plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The large flat floating leaf of a water lily is a leaf in the botanical sense.

clue.text: The rearmost in resort, one's first property?

indicators.note: read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted anew

explanation.surface: The last place in a holiday resort being somebody's first property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday town; split as re-sort it signals an anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, cheap house bought by a first-time buyer is the usual first property owned.

clue.text: Something hot produced by Marxist sergeant and bandleader?

parts.note: red is a common term for a communist or Marxist
Sgt Pepper leads the Lonely Hearts Club Band of the Beatles album

explanation.surface: A communist sergeant leads a band to produce something spicy.
explanation.definitionFit: A capsicum, especially the chilli kind, is a spicy vegetable, hot to taste.

clue.text: Editor enthralled by Greek cooking eastern rice dish

indicators.note: held captive inside the other word
cooking up letters means rearranging them

explanation.surface: An editor is captivated by a Greek cooking an eastern rice dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges Greek into KGERE, and 'enthralled by' sets the editor just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An Anglo-Indian breakfast dish of rice, smoked fish and eggs.

clue.text: Son likes playing, keeping dry in game

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the other piece inside
playing about with letters rearranges them

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry

explanation.surface: A boy enjoys playing a game while staying off alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges likes into KILES, and 'keeping' holds the teetotal letters after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub game of knocking down wooden pins with a ball, an ancestor of bowling.

clue.text: Children may be found playing it

definitions.text: Children may be found playing it

parts.words: Children may be found playing it
parts.note: in this game children hide and are then found by a seeker

explanation.surface: Children can be seen playing some game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is double-edged: you see children playing it, and in it they are literally found.
explanation.definitionFit: A children's game where one player searches for the others who have concealed themselves.

clue.text: Army doctor's source of milk in capital

parts.note: MO is a Medical Officer, an army doctor
the apostrophe s gives S
a cow gives milk

explanation.surface: An army doctor finds milk supplies in a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian capital city, a well-known example of a national capital.

clue.text: Bird, favourite on lake

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
re means on or concerning
L is a map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A pet bird sits on a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A seabird of the open ocean, such as the storm species, is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Manage to perform surgery

definitions.meaning: to run or work a business or machine
to cut into a patient as a surgeon does

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in carrying out surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both running a machine or business and a surgeon's work on a patient.

clue.text: Runs after male, just the man she'd like to marry?

definitions.text: the man she'd like to marry?

indicators.note: the runs come after the male

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
right means just or fair

explanation.surface: Someone chases a man who is simply the one she'd like to wed.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's ideal future husband is called by this jocular phrase.

clue.text: Staffs English minister's house

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it

explanation.surface: Staffordshire, an English county, holds a minister's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staffs' looks like the abbreviation of Staffordshire, an English county, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The home provided for a Presbyterian or other Scottish clergyman is the classic minister's dwelling.

clue.text: Agree to write

explanation.surface: Someone consents to send a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to match or tally, and to exchange letters with someone.

clue.text: Said in error, a lot

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone made a lot of spoken mistakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something spoken rather than written is oral, as in an oral exam.

clue.text: Everyone in wide thoroughfare in financial centre

indicators.note: the piece goes inside the other letters

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
a street is a thoroughfare
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Everyone crowds into a broad avenue in a financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: New York's financial district, home of the stock exchange, is the archetypal financial centre.

clue.text: The Parisian, extremely supercilious? To a smaller extent

parts.note: le is French for 'the', as a Parisian would say

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A Frenchman is very haughty, though perhaps not so much.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb meaning not as much is the comparative of little.
